summary: I replied to Jamshid on the early-access HSE arrangements for the 20 December survey and geotech crews, covering interim first aid, fire-fighting, the induction point and a proposed Navoi hospital and evacuation route. I flagged that the hospital is not yet confirmed and asked him to verify it. I also noted today's rain as a reason to allow weather days in the December mobilisation.

emails.subject: Early-access HSE arrangements - camp clinic, fire-fighting, induction point and medical evacuation route
emails.body:
Jamshid,

Reply to your email of 5 December and REQ-005 on the early-access HSE arrangements for the survey and geotechnical crews starting 20 December (A210, A220). Today's rain and sub-zero temperatures are a fair reminder of what we will face, so I am planning on the basis that some days will be lost and the 12 km track will be soft after rain.

1. Camp clinic. The site camp is not built until the 1 March 2027 mobilisation (M05), so there is no camp clinic in December. Interim arrangement: no clinic on site. Each survey/geotech crew (10 persons or fewer) carries one trained first aider, a first-aid kit in every vehicle, and one stretcher/blanket set in the crew lead vehicle. Casualties go straight to the nominated hospital. A permanent camp clinic and medic will be in the Rev A plan for March, and I will give you the layout with the camp plan.

2. Fire-fighting. Interim: one 6 kg ABC dry powder extinguisher in every vehicle and one 50 kg wheeled unit plus water bowser at the drilling rig and any fuel storage point. Fuel kept in approved containers only, drip trays, no fuel storage on site beyond one day's use. Fixed fire-water and the camp extinguisher scheme come with the camp in March.

3. Induction point. Interim: induction is held at the contractors' base in Navoi city before crews travel, as you require (about 60 minutes, Russian/Uzbek, English for expatriates), with cards issued by your team. A check point at the start of the 12 km track off the A-380 will check cards and log persons in and out each day. I will request a heated cabin or container for this point; if it cannot be placed before 20 December we use a vehicle-based check with a heated rest vehicle. Please confirm the induction slides and card format are ready by 17 December.

4. Nominated hospital and evacuation route. Proposal: the main regional hospital in Navoi city as the nominated hospital (ambulance 103), with the nearest district medical post as stabilisation point for minor cases. Route: work area to the 12 km access track, then onto the A-380 and into Navoi city, about 45 km. At a convoy speed of 30 km/h on the track, allow about 25 minutes for the track and about 40 minutes on the highway, so roughly 65-75 minutes in dry conditions and longer after rain. We will mark the track at each kilometre with a post number so crews can give an exact location on the radio or satellite phone. I have not yet confirmed the hospital's emergency admission capacity or a named contact, and I would like you to do this with the hospital before Rev A is issued. Until then treat the hospital as proposed, not confirmed.

5. Weather and rain. Where the track is not passable we stop the geotech rig and do not send crews. I will make the call each morning and record it in the site diary. Please include a wet-track stand-down rule in the plan.

Please confirm you agree with the above, or send comments, by 10 December so I can finalise the crew mobilisation sequence. I am copying Arun Pillai for the hospital and induction cards, and the document controller for filing.

Regards,
Sanjay Mehta
Construction Manager, Helios EPC LLC

requests.what: Confirm emergency admission capacity and a named contact at the proposed Navoi hospital, and comment on the interim first aid, fire-fighting and induction arrangements for the 20 December crews, for inclusion in HSE Plan Rev A
